text:
Aisha: Morning handoff — quick summary of overnight and current state. Woke up to two pagers: embeddings autoscaler thrash and a routing path 429 spike. Both are stabilized but still monitoring. Root causes suspected: autoscaler policy oscillation + new batcher config increasing synclat. Links/notes below.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-06-12-EMBED-AUTOSCALE (pager: paging@pagerduty) — symptoms: scaling loops 2:00-04:30 UTC, token tail latency p95 spiked to ~1.4s, customer-facing timeout errors ~0.4% requests.

Aisha: What we did overnight: scaled embeddings pool from 4 -> 8 nodes, pinned older quantized model variant for high-throughput customers, and rolled back the 2026-06-11 batcher tuning that switched to jumbo-batches. The rollback is currently in prod.

Ben: Confirming scale command used: `rctl scale pools/embeddings-high --replicas=8 --reason="autoscaler thrash"` — all nodes passed health checks at ~04:15 UTC. :thumbsup:

Chris: Routing 429s came mostly from a single egress path to region-us-west-2, we routed ~30% of traffic to fallback regional pool and applied temporary throttle-smoothing: `routerctl set-smoothing --path=egress-usw2 --alpha=0.6`. That dropped 429s to baseline by 05:00 UTC.

Janelle: Observability notes: dashboards updated — embedding-p95, autoscaler-events, and router-429s. Saved a short-run query `embedding_thrash_recent` in Grafana. Also added an alert rule to mute noisy autoscaler flapping alerts for 12h while we fix policy.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-06-12-EMBED-AUTOSCALE -> mitigated. Severity lowered to SEV3. Tracking follow-ups.

Aisha: Customer impact: small subset of high-throughput customers experienced intermittent timeouts (SLA hit for a handful of requests). No data loss. We've notified CS channel with short summary and are preparing a targeted follow-up for affected accounts.

Theo: Action items for afternoon shift: 
- Monitor autoscaler events and ensure there are no new 3+ scale-up/down loops within 6h.
- Validate that pinned model variant doesn't regress quality for customers using latest model (Chris to run quick regressions).
- Keep router smoothing in place until routing rollout is complete.
- Triage CSP audit logs for any unusual request patterns from top 5 tenants.

Chris: I'm on regression tests — running benchmark harness against sample prompts and will post results in this thread by EOD. If regressions >1% we will revert pin and instead adjust autoscaler thresholds.

Ben: Runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-thrash and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-429s — follow section "temporary-mitigation". Quick commands are copied below:
```
# scale pool
rctl scale pools/embeddings-high --replicas=8
# rollback batcher flag
deployctl rollback feature/batcher-tuning-2026-06-11
# set router smoothing
routerctl set-smoothing --path=egress-usw2 --alpha=0.6
```

Janelle: Coverage gaps: afternoon primary is Ben, secondary is Aisha until 18:00 UTC. If Ben is unavailable, page Chris (esc-level2). We currently lack an on-call owner for postmortem write-up — volunteer? :thinking_face:

Aisha: I'll take postmortem draft and share template in #postmortems. Theo, can you own follow-up with CS on affected customers?

Theo: Yep, I'll coordinate with CS and message impacted customers with timeline + mitigation steps.

incident-bot: :bell: REMINDER: open actions for INC-2026-06-12-EMBED-AUTOSCALE: [assign_postmortem], [monitor_autoscaler], [validate_pinned_model] — due 2026-06-14 12:00 UTC.

Ben: Next steps checklist for next shift: 
- Check `embedding_thrash_recent` alert (Grafana) and autoscaler event counts.
- Confirm batcher rollback remains live and batch sizes within expected range.
- Verify router 429s under 0.1% for last 30m.
- If any resurgence, escalate to Eng-Platform and open an immediate runbook meeting.

Chris: Posting initial regression results (brief): latency profile unchanged; one prompt set shows 0.8% quality drop with pinned variant — running expanded test set now, ETA 2h.

Aisha: Thanks team. Leaving the handoff here — primary Ben, secondary Aisha. Ping in this thread for quick sync or page if SEV escalates. :coffee:
